name: Cheongchun Jogae Pocha Gwangan
desc: A beloved seafood restaurant and izakaya-style eatery specializing in clams, shellfish, and grilled seafood. It’s a local favorite for late-night dining with cold drinks and lively social atmosphere close to Gwangalli Be

name: Seokhwayeon Korean BBQ
desc: A highly rated Korean barbecue restaurant in the Gwangalli area, known for generous portions of grilled meats and quality side dishes. The lively atmosphere and beachside location make it an excellent dinner choice after

name: Salmon Brothers
desc: A highly rated casual restaurant focused on salmon and seafood bowls, sushi, and creative fish dishes. Often recommended for seafood lovers looking for a more modern menu near the beach.

name: Obok Pork Soup
desc: A long-established local restaurant serving pork soup, a Busan specialty, often recommended to visitors seeking affordable and authentic regional food.

name: Millak Town Raw Fish Center
desc: Busan is famous for raw fish ('회 Hway'), which the Koreans eat in the same style as bulgogi, namely topped with kimchi and gochujang and wrapped in a lettuce leaf. One of the best places to sample this is in a large brow

name: Four Season Raw Fish
desc: The owner, Mr. Jun, speaks English, and ordering here is easy: it's either set A, B or C. Even Set A is huge, while C is extremely large. This is as real as it gets and dishes will include still-moving octopus tentacles

name: Samho Fish Restaurant
desc: A local favorite for fresh sashimi and traditional Korean seafood stews. Known for its high quality and authentic flavors, often featuring seasonal catches.

name: Ecotopia Vegetarian Restaurant
desc: Plant based Korean food in a quiet setting

name: Suyeong Dwaeji Gukbap
desc: A classic Busan-style pork and rice soup. This restaurant is in the Suyeong Gukbap alley and is known for its deep, flavorful broth.

name: Gaemijip (Gwangalli Branch)
desc: A famous Busan chain specializing in 'Nak-Gop-Sae' (spicy octopus, beef intestine, and shrimp casserole). A hearty and spicy meal, perfect for sharing.

name: Choryang Milmyeon (Suyeong)
desc: A branch of one of Busan's most famous 'milmyeon' (wheat noodle) restaurants. Offers refreshing cold noodles, both spicy (bibim) and non-spicy (mul).

name: Millak Kalguksu
desc: A humble restaurant near Millak Port serving delicious handmade noodle soup (kalguksu) and pajeon (green onion pancake).

name: Gwang-an-jip Dwaeji Galbi
desc: A long-standing local favorite for charcoal-grilled pork ribs (dwaeji galbi). The atmosphere is lively and often packed with locals.

name: La Bella Citta
desc: An upscale Italian restaurant with a direct view of the Gwangan Bridge. Specializes in pasta, risotto, and steak.

name: HQ Bar
desc: A popular expatriate-run bar with a friendly atmosphere. Serves excellent Western pub food, including burgers, wings, and fish and chips. Great selection of craft beers.

name: Burger Shop
desc: A popular gourmet burger joint. Known for its juicy, handcrafted patties and fresh ingredients. Often has a line.

name: Pizza By The Slice
desc: A casual New York-style pizzeria selling large slices. A perfect late-night snack to grab and eat by the beach.

name: Ola!
desc: A lively Spanish tapas bar serving authentic dishes like gambas al ajillo and paella. Great atmosphere with sangria and wine, plus a good view.

name: SOL Taphouse
desc: A casual pizza and pub-style restaurant serving pizzas, craft beers, and light dishes. With its beachfront proximity, it’s a popular evening gathering spot for travelers and locals.

name: Tontaro
desc: A cozy, authentic Japanese izakaya specializing in yakitori (grilled skewers) and various small dishes. Pairs well with sake or beer.

name: Bangkok in Busan
desc: Authentic Thai food restaurant run by a Thai chef. Popular for its Pad Thai and Tom Yum Goong.

name: Hanoi Phở
desc: A simple, no-frills Vietnamese restaurant serving excellent pho (beef noodle soup) and banh mi. Quick, delicious, and affordable.

name: Little Aus Cafe
desc: Australian-style cafe with variations on brunch and lunch classics.

name: Cafe Lunar
desc: A very popular cafe on the main beach road, famous for its multi-story glass windows offering unobstructed views of the bridge. Great for coffee and elaborate desserts.

name: Byul-Swae Cafe
desc: A "newtro" (new-retro) style cafe known for its quiet atmosphere and specialty hand-drip coffee.

name: Namcheon-dong Bap-ppang
desc: A bakery known for its savory breads (like onion or corn bread) and freshly baked goods. A local favorite for breakfast.

name: Terarosa Coffee Gwangalli
desc: A well-known specialty coffee café directly facing Gwangalli Beach, popular with tourists for high-quality coffee and clear views of Gwangan Bridge both during the day and at night.

name: Paul Bassett Gwangalli
desc: A premium café brand offering espresso-based drinks in a comfortable setting, often used by tourists as a rest stop while walking along the beachfront.

name: Café Knotted Gwangalli
desc: A popular dessert café known for its donuts and colorful interior, frequently visited by tourists and younger visitors walking along Gwangalli Beach.

name: Galmegi Brewery
desc: ‘The Brewery’ is Busan’s first American-style craft beer microbrewery and brewpub.

name: Thursday Party
desc: Gwangalli classic on the beach. On a good night the foosball table area becomes a dance floor and in summer the party spills onto the beach.

name: Gimbap Cheongook
desc: Serves up gimbap from ₩2000 and all sorts of noodles for ₩2500-4000. No English menu or sign, but if you can say it they'll make it, and it's open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

name: welly&food
desc: This food court serves all the usual Korean favorites, with plastic food and English menus making ordering a snap.

name: Seoul Kakkduggi
desc: Specializes in beef soups and kakkduggi side dish.

name: Amby's
desc: European, North American, Russian, and SE Asian dishes; try the borscht stew. Popular with sailors and their lady companions, the best time to go is after midnight. A small shop offering a limited selection of dust-cover

name: Eva's
desc: Turns into a bar, but they serve excellent Western food, and American-style breakfast until the afternoon. Open air bar. Thursday is ladies' bottomless drinks for ₩15000. In-Jung runs the bar and is a great hostess.

name: Leegane Tteokbokki
desc: Tteokbokki restaurant is inside the can market. Prices are reasonable at ₩5,000 for tteokbokki, ₩5,000 for fries, and ₩1,000 for a corn dog.

name: Shabana Indian Restaurant
desc: Authentic Indian restaurant owned by Indians.

name: Lee Jae Mo Pizza, Busan
desc: This is the most famous pizza restaurant in Central Busan. On weekdays and weekends, a very large number of people line up to eat inside the restaurant. To solve this problem, a take-out only store has been opened across

name: Kkangdwaehu
desc: This is a pork cutlet version of the Korean fried chicken called 'Pork Ribs Fried'. It is available in large, medium, and small sizes, with prices ranging from ₩13,000 to ₩23,000 depending on the size.

name: Donghwa Chinese Restaurant
desc: This Chinese restaurant in Busan, Jung-gu, is famous for its Yuni-jjajang and Sweet and sour pork. Noodles and fried rice are inexpensive at ₩6,000-8,000, but other dishes cost ₩20,000-30,000. Closed every Wednesday.

name: Hongudan Nampo branch
desc: It's a Chinese restaurant. Typically, there are regular course meals (₩37,000-85,000 ), lunch course meals (₩23,000-35,000), and couple course meals (₩39,000-49,000), with a 15:30 - 16:30 break.

name: Dolswe Wood-fired grilling
desc: A Korean barbecue restaurant with a single menu item: beef outside skirt It costs ₩13,000 per bowl and has sides such as Doenjangjjigae, rice, and Naengmyeon. Closed every Sunday and last order is at 21:00.

name: Club Realize
hours: Usually open on Fridays and Saturdays and sometime
desc: It's the only place to see regular metal, punk and rock in Busan. A modest amount of beer and booze at the bar is complemented by a selection of in house cocktails. Good place to go and let it all out, scream shout and g

name: Thursday Party
desc: Much akin to the other Thursday Parties in town, one of the most popular places for Koreans and Westerners to intermingle. If you've been to one, you've been to them all.

name: Kim Hee-dae Halmae Wonjo Gamasot Gukbap (Granny Kim Hee-dae'
desc: Gukbap is a hot bowl of rice and broth, and available in many of the old style restaurants in Heaundae market.

name: Bao Burger
desc: Delicious burgers in hand-made bao buns.

name: Happy Salad Club
desc: A great option if you're craving vegetables. 5 salad choices and a fruit salad for dessert.

name: Korea Red Ginseng Samgyetang Galbitang
desc: Hot broths with either chicken or beef cooked with rice and the special Korean ingredient of Ginseng.

name: Namaste
desc: Solid Indian fare in a stylish environment.

name: Fingers & Chat
desc: Really good fish and chips with fresh batter that you can eat outside by the sea. Very long queues on weekends. Also good coffee and ice cream.

name: Artista
desc: Mexican restaurant with a good reputation. Slightly out of the way, but has vegetarian options as well.

name: Ventanas Grill Steak and Seafood
desc: Novotel Ambassador, Haeundae. Steak, fresh seafood, premier wine. Sephia style interior design, cozy atmosphere, and ocean view.

name: Cola Mercato
desc: Decent Italian restaurant at the top of Dalmaji Hill with views over the ocean.

name: Outback Steakhouse
desc: Good if you want some familiar western food.

name: Obs Bakery
desc: Nice bakery with good snacks for the beach.

name: Boracay
desc: In the basement of a hotel, this is an expensive Korean style booking club.

name: Starface Bar
desc: Pool table and cool Americans aplenty on the weekends. Pretty sleepy during most weeknights.

name: Thursday Party
desc: A chain of bars in Busan and a popular place for Koreans and Westerners to intermingle.

name: U2 Bar
desc: Has live DJs and occasional live bands on weekends. Plays requests during the weekdays. Darts, pool and Hookahs available. Though not busy on most weeknights, there are usually a good mix of foreigners and Koreans inside

name: Wolfhound Irish Pub & Restaurant
desc: A proper pub serving a large variety of premium draft beers and western food. Great place for a mid week dinner and pint or to party on the weekends. Good mix of Koreans and westerners.

name: Pusan National University
desc: In the PNU area you can buy a lot of Korean student food specialties, such as Don Katsu and Croquette (Goroke - 고로케).

name: Miryang Sundae Gukbap
desc: A long-running local restaurant specializing in sundae gukbap. Popular among both residents and visitors for its rich broth and generous portions.

name: Hapcheon Dwaeji Gukbap
desc: A well-known local restaurant specializing in Busan-style pork soup, frequently recommended to visitors seeking an authentic and affordable regional dish.

name: Subyeon Chueotang
desc: A traditional Korean restaurant serving loach soup, popular among visitors interested in experiencing regional comfort food near the Nakdong River.

name: Dongnae Halmae Pajeon
desc: A famous restaurant serving Dongnae-style green onion pancakes, a regional specialty often introduced to tourists as a traditional local dish.

name: Thursday Party PNU
desc: Thursday Party is a popular pub chain in Korea, and the Pusan National University branch is famous among students for its casual atmosphere, cocktails, and affordable beer.

name: Hapcheon Illyu Dwaeji Gukbap
desc: A classic Dwaeji Gukbap, a pork soup mixed with rice restaurant.

name: Haksun Milmyeon
desc: Offers milmyeon (wheat noodles), a regional food item. Both cold noodles (mul milmyeon) and spicy mixed noodles (bibim milmyeon) are available.

name: E-eun-ji Tteok-bokki
desc: Sells tteok-bokki (spicy rice cakes) and eomuk (fish cakes). Provides a typical local street food experience.

name: Songdo Haemul Bap
desc: Serves seafood rice dishes and grilled fish options. The location provides views of the ocean and the Songdo Marine Cable Car.

name: Wonjo Halmae Nakji
desc: Specializes in nakji bokkeum (spicy stir-fried octopus) and nakgop-sae (octopus, tripe, and shrimp casserole). The dishes are noted for their high spice level.

name: Sasang Pig's Feet Alley
desc: A cluster of restaurants serving jokbal, a dish of marinated and boiled pig's feet. Various preparations, including cold sliced versions, are available.

name: Gamcheon Culture Village Snack Corner
desc: Several small vendors and cafes offering quick meals and snacks such as ramyeon (instant noodles), kimbap (seaweed rice rolls), and beverages for sightseers.

name: Dadaepo Gwangyang Sashimi
desc: Offers hoe (raw fish/sashimi) and seafood sets. The location provides a view of the ocean.

name: Pyeonghwa Dwaeji Gukbap
desc: Serves dwaeji gukbap (pork soup with rice), a staple Busan dish. Noted for its rich, clear pork broth.

name: Myeongji Jogae Changgo
desc: An all-you-can-eat establishment focusing on grilled clams and shellfish (jogae gui).

name: Dongdaeshin Kalguksu
desc: Serves handmade kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup). The broth is traditionally anchovy-based.

name: Daejeo Byeolmi Nokdu
desc: This establishment specializes in various Korean pancakes, notably the thick, savory nokdu jeon (mung bean pancake) and haemul pajeon (seafood green onion pancake). The dishes are made from freshly prepared ingredients.

name: Sasang Milmyeon
desc: A local eatery that serves milmyeon (wheat noodles), a food item associated with Busan. The restaurant offers both the chilled broth version (mul milmyeon) and the spicy mixed version (bibim milmyeon).

name: Myeongji Jangeo Maeuntang
desc: Specializes in jangeo maeuntang (spicy eel stew). The dish is served in a communal pot, combining fresh eel, vegetables, and spicy seasoning. It is a typical local favorite in the coastal region.

name: Hyeopseong Tteokgalbi
desc: Serves tteokgalbi (grilled short rib patties), which are ground, seasoned, and grilled beef or pork. The meal typically includes rice and a set of traditional side dishes (banchan).

name: Songdo Jogae House
desc: A typical seafood restaurant in the area that offers jogae gui (grilled shellfish). Patrons select their seafood, which is then cooked at the table on a charcoal grill. Operating hours are generally geared toward the eve

name: Molundae Seolleongtang
desc: This restaurant specializes in seolleongtang (ox bone soup), which is characterized by its white, milky broth from hours of slow cooking. The soup is usually served with rice and minimal seasoning, allowing diners to adj

name: Sasang Budae Jjigae
desc: The main item served here is budae jjigae (army stew), a dish cooked at the table in a large pot. Ingredients typically include ham, sausage, baked beans, kimchi, and ramen noodles in a spicy broth.

name: Joyeon-dong Haemul Kalguksu
desc: A restaurant that focuses on haemul kalguksu (seafood knife-cut noodles). The noodles are typically hand-cut and served in a broth enriched by clams, mussels, and other seasonal seafood.

name: Gangseo Hanwoo Center
desc: Operates on a unique model where guests purchase fresh cuts of Hanwoo (premium Korean beef) directly from the butcher shop section and then cook the meat themselves at tables equipped with grills.

name: Ami-dong Sundae Gukbap
desc: Serves sundae gukbap (blood sausage soup with rice). The soup contains Korean-style blood sausage (sundae) and various pork offal in a dense, rich broth. It is open at all hours.

name: Gupo Kalguksu
desc: Specializes in kalguksu (knife-cut noodles), a dish traditionally associated with the Gupo area. The noodles are typically served in a clean, anchovy-based broth. This location is one of the long-standing original stores

name: Sasang Chicken Foot Alley
desc: This alley features multiple eateries specializing in dakbal (spicy chicken feet), a popular local late-night dish. Visitors can choose between boneless or bone-in versions, usually accompanied by alcoholic beverages.

name: Songdo Haemul Tang
desc: Serves haemul tang (spicy seafood stew). The stew is prepared with a variety of fresh seasonal seafood, crabs, and shellfish in a spicy broth, designed to be shared by several people.

name: Gamcheon Donkey Steak
desc: A small, themed eatery within the cultural village serving grilled meat skewers and simple rice dishes. It is primarily geared toward tourists looking for a quick and casual meal while sightseeing.

name: Dadaepo Sundubu Jjigae
desc: Specializes in sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew). The stew is served boiling hot and can be customized with seafood or meat, accompanied by traditional side dishes. Popular as a simple breakfast or lunch option.

name: Jangeo Cheopbap (Eel Rice)
desc: The primary dish is jangeo cheopbap (grilled eel on rice), often prepared in a Japanese style with a sweet glaze. It is considered a specialty meal in the area.

name: Sasang Ttukbaegi Jjigae
desc: Offers several varieties of traditional Korean stews (jjigae) served in individual earthenware pots (ttukbaegi). Options usually include kimchi jjigae, doenjang jjigae, and sundubu jjigae.

name: Dongdaesin Bindaetteok
desc: Specializes in bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), which are traditionally pan-fried until crispy. This dish is often paired with makgeolli (Korean rice wine) and is primarily open during evening hours.

name: Myeongji Kalbi Jjim
desc: Focuses on galbi jjim (braised short ribs), a traditional slow-cooked beef or pork dish. The meat is braised in a soy sauce-based marinade with vegetables and served in a hot pot.

name: Songdo Fish BBQ
desc: A typical seaside restaurant offering various grilled whole fish (saengseon gui), such as mackerel and hairtail. The dishes are usually served as a set with rice and several small side dishes (banchan).

name: Sasang Makgeolli Alley
desc: An area containing several small, traditional pubs (jumoek) specializing in makgeolli (Korean rice wine). Various regional makgeolli types and accompanying traditional side dishes (anju) are served. This spot is popular

name: Songdo Cafe Street
desc: This street offers various cafes and pubs with views of the ocean and the Songdo Marine Cable Car. Many places serve light drinks, including craft beer and wine, alongside coffee. Suitable for those seeking a relaxing, s

name: Dadaepo Sunset Pub
desc: A casual bar offering a selection of beer and mixed drinks. Its location is utilized to provide sunset views over Dadaepo Beach, particularly popular before or after the fountain show.

name: Sasang Hoega-bar
desc: A cluster of hoega (Korean-style beer bars) that specialize in draft beer and fried chicken (chimaek). This area provides a lively, high-energy environment typical of Korean urban nightlife.

name: Gamcheon Culture Cafe Rooftop
desc: A non-alcoholic cafe that offers coffee, tea, and juice. The main draw is the high vantage point providing panoramic views of the colorful Gamcheon village houses.

name: Gudeok Traditional Tea House
desc: Serves traditional Korean teas such as sanga-cha (twin citrus tea) and sujeonggwa (cinnamon punch). This spot provides a quiet setting away from the commercial areas, suitable for daytime relaxation.

name: Myeongji Craft Beer Pub
desc: A modern pub that features a rotating selection of local and imported craft beers on tap. They also offer simple food items (anju) designed to accompany beer.

name: Toseong-dong Soju Tent
desc: An authentic Korean pojangmacha (tent bar) experience specializing in Soju and simple, hearty food. The plastic tent structure and outdoor seating are characteristic of this type of casual drinking spot.

name: Dadaepo Wine Bar
desc: A small bar that offers a curated selection of global wines, sold by the glass or bottle. It provides a quieter, more upscale alternative to the neighboring beer and soju spots.

name: Sasang Karaoke Town
price: Room rates vary / Alcohol packages requi
desc: A series of large, multi-room karaoke complexes (noraebang) that require the purchase of alcohol and food along with the room rental fee. This venue type is intended for group entertainment and late-night socializing.

name: Milyang Pork Soup
desc: Warm Pork Soup.

name: suson jjajang
desc: It is a Korean-style Chinese restaurant. Japchaebap and sweet and sour pork are delicious.

name: gaya milmyeon
desc: Delicious Wheat Noodles. Warm pork dumplings.

name: Samil Dwitgogi
desc: It sells a regional variation of Korean barbecue, called 'Dwitgogi', using unusual cuts of pork, such as jowl. 'Dwitgogi' means meat from behind, named because the cuts used to be traded unofficially from butchers, but s

name: Dohyeongmin Restaurant
desc: The main dishes of the restaurant inside and outside Gimhae, which is also famous for its Gimhae rice restaurant, include beef steak, pasta, and salad.

name: Jangwonjeong
desc: Jangwonjeong, a famous restaurant in Gimhae, is where you can enjoy hot pot rice and meat together. In particular, if you order hot pot rice, you can enjoy a generous amount of 7 side dishes made with homegrown ingredien

name: Haeru sushi
desc: Harusushi is a rotating sushi restaurant located in Nae-dong, Gimhae, and is famous for its fresh ingredients and various kinds of sushi.

name: bonghwang1935
desc: A cafe with comfortable seats and delicious coffee. The atmosphere is so good. Quiet conversation in a sedentary room.

name: Cafe Dahlia
desc: It is a cafe building that won the Grand Prize in architecture. You can enjoy tea, coffee, and bread while looking at the mountain scenery.

name: Poven
desc: Poven is a specialty bakery cafe baked by Gyeongsangnam-do masters.

name: Fruits Forest
desc: The main branch of Fruit Forest is a cafe in Gimhae that offers a variety of desserts and drinks using fresh fruits.
